    Screen every engine on one cohort

    Source: R/model.R
    sdt_workflowset.Rd

    Fits each available engine to the same data with the same preprocessing and the same resamples, and returns a leaderboard. This is the whole bench: glass-box and black-box models scored side by side, so the price of interpretability is a number rather than an opinion.

    Usage

    sdt_workflowset(
  data,
  target = c("triage", "therapy", "called_triage", "called_therapy"),
  engines = NULL,
  predictors = NULL,
  tune = TRUE,
  grid = 5L,
  folds = 5L,
  prop = 0.75,
  parallel = FALSE,
  workers = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

    Arguments

    data

    A cohort or data frame of casualties.

    target

    Outcome to predict. "triage" and "therapy" are the true values on the card; "called_triage" and "called_therapy" are what a participant assigned, as produced by sdt_add_decisions(). The true values are close to a deterministic function of the card, so every engine scores near 1 on them and the comparison is uninformative. The participant's call is the target worth benchmarking.

    engines

    Which engines to screen. Defaults to all of them.

    predictors

    Character vector of predictor columns. Defaults to the card fields, excluding identifiers and every outcome column, so a model for the participant's call cannot simply read the true category.

    tune

    If TRUE, tune hyperparameters over a grid; if FALSE, fit the specification's defaults once.

    grid

    Number of candidate hyperparameter settings.

    folds

    Number of cross-validation folds, stratified on the target.

    prop

    Proportion of the data used for training in the initial split.

    parallel

    If TRUE, fit resamples and grid points in parallel. Defaults to FALSE: a package that claims every core without being asked is a bad guest on a shared machine, and a sequential run needs no thought about RNG streams. It pays off on a tuned fit or an engine screen and costs a little on a single untuned one. The backend is set up for the duration of the call and the caller's plan is restored on exit.

    workers

    Number of parallel workers, or NULL to choose one: a core short of the machine, capped at 8.

    seed

    Optional integer seed, applied with withr::local_seed().

    verbose

    If TRUE, report progress via cli.

    Value

    A tibble::tibble() with one row per engine and metric: engine, class_box, .metric, .estimator, .estimate, ranked with the best roc_auc first. Carries a skipped attribute listing engines that could not be fitted here, and a models attribute holding the fitted sdt_model objects.

    Details

    Engines whose package is not installed are skipped, and named in the skipped attribute rather than silently dropped. So is the transformer when keras3 is installed but has no working backend.

    See also

    sdt_fit(), sdt_metrics().

    Examples

    co <- sdt_synthetic_cohort(n = 150, seed = 4)
needed <- c("parsnip", "recipes", "workflows", "rsample", "tune",
            "yardstick", "rpart")
if (all(vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE))) {
  sdt_workflowset(co, target = "triage", engines = "tree",
                  tune = FALSE, seed = 1, verbose = FALSE)
}
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   engine class_box .metric  .estimator .estimate
#>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr>    <chr>          <dbl>
#> 1 tree   glass     accuracy multiclass         1
#> 2 tree   glass     f_meas   macro              1
#> 3 tree   glass     kap      multiclass         1
#> 4 tree   glass     roc_auc  hand_till          1
